newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may speed up foreign fund liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may speed up foreign fund liberalisation.

text.p: Taiwan's Finance Minister Paul Chiu said the government may speed up liberalisation of foreign investment in the stock market before the 2000 deadline, the Economic Daily News reported on Sunday.
It quoted Chiu as saying the Finance Ministry did not rule out the possibility of lifting all restrictions on foreign funds before 2000.
The reforms might be pushed ahead according to actual demand in the market. He did not elaborate.
The report said Chiu's comment would boost already buoyant share prices, which surged to a 22-month high at 6,842.16 at the Saturday close on turnover of T$103 billion.
The government plans to gradually remove barriers to foreign investment in Taiwan's financial markets as part of its drive to develop the island into an Asia-Pacific financial centre.
Current curbs on foreign ownership of local shares are designed to ensure local control and maintain the stability of local financial markets, but the government pledged to phase them out by 2000.
The Securities and Exchange Commission last week raised the limit on foreign ownership of Taiwan stock-market equity to 25 percent from 20 percent.
The ceiling on a single foreign investment in any listed company was raised to 10 percent from 7.5 percent.
Foreign fund inflows have accelerated since Morgan Stanley Capital International began weighting Taiwan's stock index in its global emerging markets index on September 2.
